name: primitives-texts-sliding-number

frames.best_why: The large counter is nearly legible and both smaller counters sit below it.

tagline: Each digit rolls upward like an odometer wheel to the next number.
summary: A live number display whose digits spring vertically to their new value, with columns of numerals sliding past inside fixed slots. The demo runs three sizes, including a comma-grouped and a two-decimal version.
appearance: A large bold white number sits centred on a near-black stage with a small grey caption under it. Below are two smaller counters side by side, one with commas and one with decimals, each with its own tiny caption.
behaviour: Every 1.8 seconds the number changes and each digit column springs upward or downward, showing a short stack of passing numerals before coming to rest on the new digit. Thousands and decimal points stay put while the digits move.
demo_content: Counters labelled Sliding digits, with separator and decimal cycle through 1234, 5678, 9999, 42 and 3141.
search_phrases: number rolls up like an odometer
digits spin to the next value
count up numbers with stacked digits
use_when: A dashboard metric or KPI changes value and the change should read as motion rather than a jump.
avoid_when: Very fast or constant updates: overlapping springs make the digits unreadable.
customise: Number, starting value, decimal places and separators are props, as is the spring; restyling the digit wheels needs a source edit.
weight_why: Ten absolutely positioned digit spans per column driven by one spring; idle between changes.

a11y.note: Digits are real text, but value changes are not announced and there is no reduced-motion fallback.

issues: No frame catches the counters at rest; every one is sampled mid-roll.
polish_why: Convincing odometer spring, but every sampled frame is mid-motion and captions are faint.
